hero.title: Diamond Star Motors
hero.subtitle: Chrysler and Mitsubishi's joint venture combined U.S. manufacturing might with Japan's turbocharged Sirius engineering to create a 1990s performance icon.

about.title: THE PARTNERSHIP
about.subtitle: How two automotive giants joined forces to create a legend
about.headline: A Groundbreaking Alliance
paragraphs: Chrysler's 1970 purchase of a 15% stake in Mitsubishi opened the door for rebadged Mitsubishis to fill America's demand for efficient compacts. By the early 1980s both companies were clashing with import quotas and dealership restrictions, making a U.S.-built solution essential.

Diamond Star Motors formally launched in October 1985 as an equal partnership. Construction of a 1.9-million-square-foot plant in Normal, Illinois began the following April, and by March 1988 the automated facility—complete with roughly 1,000 robots—was ready to assemble up to 240,000 cars per year.

Production kicked off in 1989 with the Eclipse, Talon, and Laser triplets, all built around Mitsubishi's turbo-ready Sirius engines and the now-celebrated 4G63. Mitsubishi purchased Chrysler's stake in 1991, the plant was renamed Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America in 1995, and the site continued producing models until its closure in 2015.

precursors.introDescription: Before DSM, Mitsubishi refined a family of turbocharged fours that set the stage for the 4G63. From the compact 4G61T to the rally-proven early 4G63 and the Starion's track lessons, each iteration sharpened the formula that DSM would perfect.

cards.title: 4G61 Turbo (Sirius Family)
cards.description: This 1.6L turbocharged sibling to the 4G63 powered the Mitsubishi Colt and Mirage. Its DOHC layout, forced induction, and robust bottom end previewed the engineering blueprint that DSM would inherit.

cards.title: Lancer EX 2000 Turbo
cards.description: The first production car to showcase the turbocharged 4G63 merged Group 4 rally ambition with a street chassis. It validated the iron-block's durability and multi-valve head that DSM tuners still celebrate.

cards.title: Mitsubishi Starion / Chrysler Conquest
cards.description: Mitsubishi's rear-drive turbo coupe and its Chrysler-branded twins proved the Sirius block could handle boost and track abuse. The car's motorsport data fed directly into DSM chassis and powertrain tuning.

cards.title: Astron & Saturn Foundations
cards.description: Mitsubishi's earlier Astron and Saturn engines introduced balance shafts, aluminum heads, and turbocharging lessons that carried into the Sirius program, ensuring DSM's 4G63 could balance smoothness with strength.

timeline.title: THE HISTORY
timeline.subtitle: Key corporate milestones in the Diamond Star Motors journey

events.title: Chrysler Invests in Mitsubishi
events.description: Chrysler acquires a 15% stake in Mitsubishi Motors, opening the U.S. market to rebadged Mitsubishi imports under Chrysler, Dodge, and Plymouth badges.

events.title: Import Quota Pressures
events.description: Voluntary restraints on Japanese-branded cars and Mitsubishi's desire for its own U.S. dealers push both companies toward a domestic production solution.

events.title: Diamond Star Motors Incorporated
events.description: Chrysler and Mitsubishi create DSM as a 50-50 joint venture to combine engineering resources and bypass import limits.

events.title: Groundbreaking in Normal, Illinois
events.description: Construction begins on a 1.9 million square-foot factory financed with state and local incentives to build up to 240,000 vehicles annually.

events.title: Plant Completed
events.description: DSM finishes its highly automated plant, integrating around 1,000 robots with a skilled workforce to launch U.S.-built production.

events.title: Production Begins
events.description: The Mitsubishi Eclipse, Plymouth Laser, and Eagle Talon—collectively known as the DSM triplets—roll off the line, highlighting turbocharged performance options.

events.title: UAW Local 2488 Forms
events.description: Factory employees organize as UAW Local 2488 and sign their first labor contract with Diamond Star Motors.

events.title: Mitsubishi Takes Full Control
events.description: Financial pressures lead Chrysler to sell its 50% share to Mitsubishi, though Chrysler-branded models continue under contract manufacturing.

events.title: Renamed Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America
events.description: DSM's corporate identity sunsets as Mitsubishi rebrands the facility, even as enthusiasts keep the DSM nickname alive.

events.title: North American Manufacturing Division
events.description: A second rebranding to Mitsubishi Motors North America, Manufacturing Division reflects broader corporate integration.

events.title: End of Vehicle Production
events.description: Mitsubishi ceases manufacturing at the Normal, Illinois plant, closing the original DSM assembly line.

intro.title: Sirius Roots, 4G63 Brilliance
intro.description: The DSM legend is inseparable from Mitsubishi's Sirius engine family. Innovations from the 4G61T and early 4G63 programs powered rally wins, sports coupes, and today’s record-setting builds.

milestones.title: Sirius Engine Family Debuts
milestones.description: Mitsubishi introduces the multi-valve Sirius line, culminating in the 4G6x series that would anchor DSM performance.

milestones.title: Lancer EX 2000 Turbo
milestones.description: The first turbocharged 4G63 appears in the Lancer EX 2000 Turbo, proving the platform's racing credentials.

milestones.title: Starion & Conquest Development
milestones.description: Rear-drive Starion and Chrysler Conquest models refine turbocharging, intercooling, and durability lessons used by DSM engineers.

milestones.title: Galant VR-4 Rally Pedigree
milestones.description: Group A rally success shows the 4G63T can withstand international motorsport punishment while delivering AWD confidence.

milestones.title: DSM Triplets
milestones.description: Eclipse, Talon, and Laser enthusiasts embrace the 4G63T's stout bottom end and tuning ceiling, launching a global tuner movement.

milestones.title: Lancer Evolution Era
milestones.description: Successive Lancer Evolution models keep the 4G63 winning, highlighted by Tommi Mäkinen's four consecutive WRC drivers' titles.

tabs.label: Sirius Family
tabs.intro: Direct ancestors within the Sirius 4G6x family laid every piece of hardware that DSM tuners rely on today.

bullets.title: 4G61 Turbo
bullets.text: Compact 1.6L turbo in the Colt/Mirage proved the architecture could handle boost and DOHC breathing.

bullets.title: 4G67 1.8L
bullets.text: Naturally aspirated and performance variants showed the valvetrain flexibility later shared with the 4G63.

bullets.title: Early 4G63T
bullets.text: First fitted to the Lancer EX 2000 Turbo and Starion rally cars, combining iron-block strength with multi-valve heads.

tabs.label: Earlier Families
tabs.intro: Before Sirius, Mitsubishi experimented with balance shafts and alloy heads that shaped the 4G63's manners.

bullets.title: Astron (4G5x)
bullets.text: Popularized the Silent Shaft balancing system and big-bore turbo blocks that inspired Sirius bottom-end durability.

bullets.title: Saturn (4G3x)
bullets.text: Introduced lightweight aluminum OHC designs and efficient combustion chambers adopted by later engines.

bullets.title: Orion Series
bullets.text: Compact overhead-cam fours for small Mitsubishis provided packaging and emissions lessons.

tabs.label: Turbo Era Inspiration
tabs.intro: Motorsport and showroom turbo programs of the 1980s sharpened Mitsubishi's forced-induction playbook.

bullets.title: Group A Rally
bullets.text: Galant VR-4 and early Lancer Evolutions validated the AWD turbo formula that DSM models embraced.

bullets.title: Starion Racing
bullets.text: IMSA and touring-car campaigns stressed intercooling, fueling, and durability upgrades used in DSM calibrations.

bullets.title: Street Performance
bullets.text: Turbocharged Lancers, Starions, and Colts built the enthusiast expectations DSM would exceed in the 1990s.
